Reg. 5 Interpretation. 'Serious incident' means an incident resulting in death, injury requiring hospital admission, loss of a vessel, or a pollution release exceeding the threshold in Schedule 2. 'Reportable incident' means any incident listed in Schedule 3.

Reg. 6 Duty to keep records. Every operator shall keep a log of all incidents, whether or not reportable, for at least five years.

Reg. 7 Notification. (1) The operator shall notify the Authority of a serious incident within 24 hours of becoming aware of it. (2) The operator shall notify the Authority of any other reportable incident within 15 days. (3) Notification shall be made using the form published by the Authority.

Reg. 8 Investigation. The Authority may appoint an inspector to investigate any incident notified under regulation 7 and the operator shall give the inspector reasonable access to premises, vessels and records.

Reg. 9 Offences. An operator who fails without reasonable excuse to comply with regulation 7 commits an offence.

Schedule 3 (extract). Reportable incidents include: collisions between vessels; groundings; fires on board; failure of mooring equipment; any fall of a person into the water.

Schedule 2 (extract). Pollution release thresholds: oil or oily mixtures, 100 litres; hazardous noxious substances, any quantity listed in Part B; sewage from vessels within harbour limits, any quantity. Releases below these thresholds must still be logged under regulation 6.

state.brief_text: Section 14(3) of the Tenancy Deposits Act requires landlords to return deposits within 10 days of the tenancy ending.

statute_excerpt.14(1): A landlord who receives a deposit shall protect it in an approved scheme within 30 days of receipt.
statute_excerpt.14(2): The landlord shall return the deposit, less any agreed deductions, within 10 days of the date on which the tenancy ends.
statute_excerpt.14(3): Where the parties dispute any deduction, the disputed amount shall be retained in the scheme until the dispute is resolved.
statute_excerpt.14(4): A landlord who fails to comply with subsection (1) or (2) is liable to pay the tenant a sum not exceeding three times the deposit.

state:
Exhibit label: In his letter of October 1862, farmer Tobias Wren wrote that the harvest had "failed entirely".

Cited source - transcription of letter, Wren family papers, box 3 (spelling modernised):

Hollin Farm, 14th October 1862

My dear Martha,

I write in haste, as the carrier leaves at noon and I would not have you wait another week for news. Your mother is much recovered and was able to sit in the garden on Sunday, though the doctor still forbids her the stairs. The children are well, and young Tom has begun at the school in Easterby, where the master reports him quick at figures but idle at his letters.

As to the farm: the barley has failed entirely, the rain having lain on it through August so that much of it sprouted in the ear, and what we saved is fit only for the pigs. The wheat, thank God, is better than we feared; we had it in before the worst of the weather, and I think it will pay the rent at Lady Day if prices hold. The turnips are small but sound. We have sold the grey mare to Mr. Garrow for less than she was worth, as I could not afford to keep her through the winter.

There is talk in the village of a new chapel, and your aunt has been collecting subscriptions with great energy. The railway surveyors were seen again on the top road, though nobody knows what comes of it.

Write when you can, and tell me whether you have found a place for the winter. I remain your loving brother,

Tobias Wren

state.design_doc_claim: The Helix protocol requires clients to retry a failed request at most three times (Helix Spec, s. 6.1).

spec_section.title: Retry behaviour
spec_section.text: Clients SHOULD NOT retry a failed request more than three times. Clients MUST use exponential backoff between retries and MUST NOT retry requests that failed with a 4xx status. The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD and SHOULD NOT are to be interpreted as described in section 1.3.

criteria: Governs exactly the behaviour the claim describes

verdict.note: The limit is right, but it is a SHOULD NOT, not a requirement; many engineers read the two loosely.
